item.title: Bros ‘n Dough receives $5,000 from Spirit of Main Street grant program - Oxford Leader
item.description: OXFORD — Bros ‘n Dough received a $5,000 check from the Spirit of Main Street grant program on March 10. The company, owned by Angie Green, is taking the bagel bombs sold at Evergreens Coffee and Bakeshop and selling them to grocery stores. item.title: Resident appreciates Oxford school board questioning proposed county millage - Oxford Leader
item.description: Dear Editor, I want to express my appreciation to the Oxford school board for its willingness to question the proposed 1.5-mill county-wide property tax scheduled for the August ballot. item.title: Michigan Press Association urges lawmakers to prioritize transparency, protect public notice requirements - Oxford Leader
item.description: During Sunshine Week (March 15-21), which highlights the importance of public records and open government, the Michigan Press Association is urging state lawmakers to prioritize trans­parency and maintain accountability measures that help keep residents informed and engaged. item.title: The Oxford RoboCats finish as District Event Finalist at Milford competition - Oxford Leader
item.description: The Oxford Robocats, Team 2137, won the Autonomous Award and District Finalist Award during the district robotics competition at Milford over the weekend. The RoboCats alliance finished second in the competition and will compete March 28-29 in Mason, Michigan. See the story on page 10.
